description: U.S. Department of Commerce | NOAA | Acquisition and Grants Office REQUEST FOR INFORMATION U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis Issue date: November 18, 2026 Responses due: December 2, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. EST / 5:00 p.m. MST Questions requested by: November 24, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. EST / noon MST Responses and questions: Email both contacts below. Kyle Shaffer, Contracting Officer | kyle.shaffer@noaa.gov Nicholas Brown, Contract Specialist | nicholas.g.brown@noaa.gov Issuing office: NOAA Acquisition and Grants Office, Western Acquisition Division - Boulder 1. Purpose and acquisition status NOAA seeks information from firms capable of performing seafood supply-chain mapping, risk analysis, and complex data analysis for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), Office of International Affairs, Trade, and Commerce (IATC). Responses will help NOAA refine the requirement, assess available expertise, identify data and access needs, inform budget planning and the independent Government cost estimate (IGCE), and determine an acquisition approach. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation. NOAA does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI and will not pay for the information requested or response preparation. Responses are information only, not quotations or offers. NOAA may or may not issue a solicitation. A response is not required to participate in a future competition. Responses are welcome from all interested sources, including small and other-than-small businesses. The acquisition vehicle and set-aside for a future procurement have not been determined. NAICS 541690 is the preliminary classification. Respondents may recommend another code with an explanation. 2. Background and objectives IATC administers the Seafood Import Monitoring Program (SIMP) and supports trade policy initiatives concerning U.S. seafood exports. SIMP uses harvest, landing, and chain-of-custody information to help detect and deter illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and misrepresentation in seafood entering the U.S. market. NOAA seeks analytical support to: Map supply chains. Further develop existing mapping and identify custodians at each node from harvest through U.S. import, including U.S. territories. Prioritize and analyze risk. Identify priority supply chains and examine species covered by SIMP and other species of NMFS interest for IUU-fishing and misrepresentation risks. Analyze U.S. re-imports. Examine processing and market dynamics for U.S.-sourced seafood and imports that directly compete with key U.S. seafood products. 3. Data, equipment, and onboarding assumptions Use the following assumptions when describing capability, schedule, and resource needs. They describe NOAA's current planning, not final contract terms or authorization to access data. Identify any assumption that would prevent performance or materially affect the proposed approach. Period of performance. NOAA is planning completion of all four milestones within 12 months of the contract or task-order effective date, including onboarding, analysis, and Government review. Respondents should address the feasibility of this schedule and opportunities for earlier completion. Data and systems. The planned environment includes NOAA Fisheries instances of BigQuery and Looker, and Government Google Workspace tools such as Sheets, Docs, and Drive. NOAA anticipates providing aggregated key-data-element tables, relevant importer documents used in SIMP audits, existing work products, data architecture guides, and field definitions. Public sources include Census trade data and the NOAA Fisheries foreign trade portal. Individual access would depend on need-to-know, required nondisclosure agreements, and security approval. Equipment and approved tools. For planning, assume project work, data, and deliverables remain on NOAA-furnished laptops and approved Government systems, not contractor-owned devices. The initial equipment planning basis is five laptops, not a staffing minimum or maximum. Additional equipment needs may be identified but are not guaranteed. R and R Shiny are contemplated tools, with installation by the NOAA Fisheries Help Desk. Do not assume permission to install unapproved software or use a new service. Recommended alternatives may be identified for Government consideration. Data protection and transmission. Plan to exchange protected project information through Kiteworks or another NOAA-approved secure method, not ordinary email alone. Explain how employees, subcontractors, and subject-matter experts would work within the same access and information-handling restrictions. Artificial intelligence tools. Trade-confidential data from BigQuery or Looker must not be used in AI tools. Public-data use in NOAA Fisheries' Gemini environment may be considered subject to Government approval. Do not assume approval for other AI tools. Identify any proposed use and the data involved. Onboarding and continuity. For schedule comparison, use a planning allowance of 60 to 90 calendar days for Public Trust processing, followed by approximately one to two weeks for account provisioning and equipment readiness after security approval when equipment is available. These are response-planning assumptions, not guaranteed processing times. Additional equipment or replacement personnel may require more time. Identify the schedule effect of delays and the work that could proceed without protected data or system access. The public NMFS Partner Government Agency (PGA) Message Set Guidelines describe reporting fields and data relationships; they do not make the underlying import or audit records public. No access to non-public data or analysis of actual NOAA records is requested in response to this RFI. NMFS PGA Message Set Guidelines https://www.cbp.gov/document/guidance/nmfs-pga-message-set-guidelines 4. Proposed milestones and billing approach NOAA is considering firm-fixed-price services with payments tied to Government acceptance of the following milestone outputs. The milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment terms are not final. Respondents should identify practical improvements. I. Initial mapping and data development Onboard, review existing work, and complete or refine initial supply-chain mapping, including source fisheries, landing locations, and primary processing entities. Provide a data table suitable for BigQuery and an electronic summary of the work completed and initial supply chains identified for further analysis. II. Prioritized supply chains Develop the list of priority supply chains for further analysis, building on the Government-provided mapping. Provide the prioritization document and supporting documentation, including the source-fishery, landing, and primary-processing information used. III. Near-final mapping and analysis Provide updated supply-chain mapping, analysis of priority supply chains, and re-import analysis. Include an updated BigQuery data table, supporting analytical materials, and research and summaries of source-fishery regulations and laws, including harvesting nations' legal species and harvesting methods relevant to U.S. imports. IV. Final reports and data Complete internal and public reports with visuals, supporting documentation, and the final BigQuery data table containing supply-chain mapping and additional analysis. Reports and supporting documents are contemplated as electronic deliverables. Any hard-copy requirement would be specified in a solicitation. 5. Information requested Provide a company information sheet and a narrative addressing the numbered questions below. Use the question numbers and state the assumptions behind each response. Brief, specific answers are preferred to general marketing materials. No completed analysis, detailed technical proposal, or binding price quotation is requested. Company information sheet. description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District will be issuing Invitation for Bids for the Wareham Harbor Federal Navigation Project, located in Wareham, Massachusetts. This procurement is a Small Business Set Aside Invitation for Bid (IFB). The NAICS code for the work is 237990 with a size standard of $37M. Construction is expected to take about five months to complete. The estimated construction cost is $1,000,000 to $5,000,000. Any responsible source meeting this standard may submit a bid to be considered by the New England District. The Wareham Harbor FNP consists of a 2.4 mile long, 9-foot deep Mean Lower Low Water (MLLW) channel. The channel is comprised of several reaches of varying widths (100-ft to 250-ft widths) to include the entrance channel through Cromeset Neck Reach, Quahaug Bar Reach, Parkwood Beach Reach, and the Inner Harbor Reach. The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging up to appropriately 52,000 cubic yards (CY) of shoaled material over a 10.2-acre area. Most of the material is fine-grained/silt and will be transported by scow and placed at Cape Cod Bay Disposal Site (CCBDS), approximately 35 miles away. Transit from Wareham to CCBDS will occur through the Cape Cod Canal. A smaller portion of the material is sand (approx. 1,000 CY) and will be placed beneficially at a nearshore site off of Church's Beach in Cuttyhunk, Massachusetts (approximately 28 miles away). Dredging operations can start on July 1, 2026 for maintenance dredging using a mechanical dredge and placement in open water at CCBDS and Church�s Beach Nearshore Placement Site. All work must be complete by December 31, 2026. In order to accomplish all dredging requirements within the specified dredging window the Contractor will need to meet a production rate of at least 28,500 CY per 30 consecutive calendar day period. This is not an invitation for bids at this time. The solicitation requirements and contract documents to include instructions for submission and the response date will be available on or about mid-November 2025. Neither telephonic, mailed nor faxed requests for hard copies of this solicitation will be accepted. The solicitation will only be available online; in order to download the solicitation offerors must access the System of Award Management website (https://www.sam.gov/) and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (https://piee.eb.mil/). All responsible sources may submit a bid which shall be considered by the New England District. Additional questions may be emailed to the Contract Specialist at heather.m.skorik@usace.army.mil. title: U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis
description: U.S. Department of Commerce | NOAA | Acquisition and Grants Office REQUEST FOR INFORMATION U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis Issue date: November 18, 2026 Responses due: December 2, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. EST / 5:00 p.m. MST Questions requested by: November 24, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. EST / noon MST Responses and questions: Email both contacts below. Kyle Shaffer, Contracting Officer | kyle.shaffer@noaa.gov Nicholas Brown, Contract Specialist | nicholas.g.brown@noaa.gov Issuing office: NOAA Acquisition and Grants Office, Western Acquisition Division - Boulder 1. Purpose and acquisition status NOAA seeks information from firms capable of performing seafood supply-chain mapping, risk analysis, and complex data analysis for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), Office of International Affairs, Trade, and Commerce (IATC). Responses will help NOAA refine the requirement, assess available expertise, identify data and access needs, inform budget planning and the independent Government cost estimate (IGCE), and determine an acquisition approach. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation. NOAA does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI and will not pay for the information requested or response preparation. Responses are information only, not quotations or offers. NOAA may or may not issue a solicitation. A response is not required to participate in a future competition. Responses are welcome from all interested sources, including small and other-than-small businesses. The acquisition vehicle and set-aside for a future procurement have not been determined. NAICS 541690 is the preliminary classification. Respondents may recommend another code with an explanation. 2. Background and objectives IATC administers the Seafood Import Monitoring Program (SIMP) and supports trade policy initiatives concerning U.S. seafood exports. SIMP uses harvest, landing, and chain-of-custody information to help detect and deter illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and misrepresentation in seafood entering the U.S. market. NOAA seeks analytical support to: Map supply chains. Further develop existing mapping and identify custodians at each node from harvest through U.S. import, including U.S. territories. Prioritize and analyze risk. Identify priority supply chains and examine species covered by SIMP and other species of NMFS interest for IUU-fishing and misrepresentation risks. Analyze U.S. re-imports. Examine processing and market dynamics for U.S.-sourced seafood and imports that directly compete with key U.S. seafood products. 3. Data, equipment, and onboarding assumptions Use the following assumptions when describing capability, schedule, and resource needs. They describe NOAA's current planning, not final contract terms or authorization to access data. Identify any assumption that would prevent performance or materially affect the proposed approach. Period of performance. NOAA is planning completion of all four milestones within 12 months of the contract or task-order effective date, including onboarding, analysis, and Government review. Respondents should address the feasibility of this schedule and opportunities for earlier completion. Data and systems. The planned environment includes NOAA Fisheries instances of BigQuery and Looker, and Government Google Workspace tools such as Sheets, Docs, and Drive. NOAA anticipates providing aggregated key-data-element tables, relevant importer documents used in SIMP audits, existing work products, data architecture guides, and field definitions. Public sources include Census trade data and the NOAA Fisheries foreign trade portal. Individual access would depend on need-to-know, required nondisclosure agreements, and security approval. Equipment and approved tools. For planning, assume project work, data, and deliverables remain on NOAA-furnished laptops and approved Government systems, not contractor-owned devices. The initial equipment planning basis is five laptops, not a staffing minimum or maximum. Additional equipment needs may be identified but are not guaranteed. R and R Shiny are contemplated tools, with installation by the NOAA Fisheries Help Desk. Do not assume permission to install unapproved software or use a new service. Recommended alternatives may be identified for Government consideration. Data protection and transmission. Plan to exchange protected project information through Kiteworks or another NOAA-approved secure method, not ordinary email alone. Explain how employees, subcontractors, and subject-matter experts would work within the same access and information-handling restrictions. Artificial intelligence tools. Trade-confidential data from BigQuery or Looker must not be used in AI tools. Public-data use in NOAA Fisheries' Gemini environment may be considered subject to Government approval. Do not assume approval for other AI tools. Identify any proposed use and the data involved. Onboarding and continuity. For schedule comparison, use a planning allowance of 60 to 90 calendar days for Public Trust processing, followed by approximately one to two weeks for account provisioning and equipment readiness after security approval when equipment is available. These are response-planning assumptions, not guaranteed processing times. Additional equipment or replacement personnel may require more time. Identify the schedule effect of delays and the work that could proceed without protected data or system access. The public NMFS Partner Government Agency (PGA) Message Set Guidelines describe reporting fields and data relationships; they do not make the underlying import or audit records public. No access to non-public data or analysis of actual NOAA records is requested in response to this RFI. NMFS PGA Message Set Guidelines https://www.cbp.gov/document/guidance/nmfs-pga-message-set-guidelines 4. Proposed milestones and billing approach NOAA is considering firm-fixed-price services with payments tied to Government acceptance of the following milestone outputs. The milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment terms are not final. Respondents should identify practical improvements. I. Initial mapping and data development Onboard, review existing work, and complete or refine initial supply-chain mapping, including source fisheries, landing locations, and primary processing entities. Provide a data table suitable for BigQuery and an electronic summary of the work completed and initial supply chains identified for further analysis. II. Prioritized supply chains Develop the list of priority supply chains for further analysis, building on the Government-provided mapping. Provide the prioritization document and supporting documentation, including the source-fishery, landing, and primary-processing information used. III. Near-final mapping and analysis Provide updated supply-chain mapping, analysis of priority supply chains, and re-import analysis. Include an updated BigQuery data table, supporting analytical materials, and research and summaries of source-fishery regulations and laws, including harvesting nations' legal species and harvesting methods relevant to U.S. imports. IV. Final reports and data Complete internal and public reports with visuals, supporting documentation, and the final BigQuery data table containing supply-chain mapping and additional analysis. Reports and supporting documents are contemplated as electronic deliverables. Any hard-copy requirement would be specified in a solicitation. 5. description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION / SOURCES SOUGHT U.S. Seafood Supply-Chain Mapping, Risk Analysis, and Re-Import Analysis Issue date: November 18, 2026 Responses due: December 02, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Mountain Standard Time (MST) Questions requested by: November 24, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. MST Responses and questions: Email both contacts below. Kyle Shaffer, Contracting Officer | kyle.shaffer@noaa.gov Nicholas Brown, Contract Specialist | nicholas.g.brown@noaa.gov Issuing office: NOAA Acquisition and Grants Office, Western Acquisition Division - Boulder Purpose and acquisition status NOAA seeks information from firms capable of performing seafood supply-chain mapping, risk analysis, and complex data analysis for the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), Office of International Affairs, Trade, and Commerce (IATC). Responses will help NOAA refine the requirement, assess available expertise, identify data and access needs, inform budget planning and the independent Government cost estimate (IGCE), and determine an acquisition approach. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation. NOAA does not intend to award a contract based on this RFI and will not pay for the information requested or response preparation. Responses are information only, not quotations or offers. NOAA may or may not issue a solicitation. A response is not required to participate in a future competition. Responses are welcome from small and other-than-small businesses and other interested organizations. Participation is not limited to holders of GSA or NOAA ProTech contracts. NOAA has not selected an acquisition vehicle or made a set-aside determination. NAICS 541715 is the preliminary classification; 541990 is an alternative under consideration. Respondents may recommend another code with an explanation. Background and objectives IATC administers the Seafood Import Monitoring Program (SIMP) and supports trade policy initiatives concerning U.S. seafood exports. SIMP uses harvest, landing, and chain-of-custody information to help detect and deter illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and misrepresentation in seafood entering the U.S. market. NOAA seeks analytical support to: Map supply chains. Further develop existing mapping and identify custodians at each node from harvest through U.S. import, including U.S. territories. Prioritize and analyze risk. Identify priority supply chains and examine species covered by SIMP and other species of NMFS interest for IUU-fishing and misrepresentation risks. Analyze U.S. re-imports. Examine processing and market dynamics for U.S.-sourced seafood and imports that directly compete with key U.S. seafood products. Data, equipment, and onboarding assumptions Use the following assumptions when describing capability, schedule, and resource needs. They describe NOAA's current planning, not final contract terms or authorization to access data. Identify any assumption that would prevent performance or materially affect the proposed approach. Period of performance. NOAA is planning completion of all four milestones within 12 months of the contract or task-order effective date, including onboarding, analysis, and Government review. Respondents should address the feasibility of this schedule and opportunities for earlier completion. Data and systems. The planned environment includes NOAA Fisheries instances of BigQuery and Looker, and Government Google Workspace tools such as Sheets, Docs, and Drive. NOAA anticipates providing aggregated key-data-element tables, relevant importer documents used in SIMP audits, existing work products, data architecture guides, and field definitions. Public sources include Census trade data and the NOAA Fisheries foreign trade portal. Individual access would depend on need-to-know, required nondisclosure agreements, and security approval. Equipment and approved tools. For planning, assume project work, data, and deliverables remain on NOAA-furnished laptops and approved Government systems, not contractor-owned devices. The initial equipment planning basis is five laptops, not a staffing minimum or maximum. Additional equipment needs may be identified but are not guaranteed. R and R Shiny are contemplated tools, with installation by the NOAA Fisheries Help Desk. Do not assume permission to install unapproved software or use a new service. Recommended alternatives may be identified for Government consideration. Data protection and transmission. Plan to exchange protected project information through Kiteworks or another NOAA-approved secure method, not ordinary email alone. Explain how employees, subcontractors, and subject-matter experts would work within the same access and information-handling restrictions. Artificial intelligence tools. Trade-confidential data from BigQuery or Looker must not be used in AI tools. Public-data use in NOAA Fisheries' Gemini environment may be considered subject to Government approval. Do not assume approval for other AI tools. Identify any proposed use and the data involved. Onboarding and continuity. For schedule comparison, use a planning allowance of 60 to 90 calendar days for Public Trust processing, followed by approximately one to two weeks for account provisioning and equipment readiness after security approval when equipment is available. These are response-planning assumptions, not guaranteed processing times. Additional equipment or replacement personnel may require more time. Identify the schedule effect of delays and the work that could proceed without protected data or system access. The public NMFS Partner Government Agency (PGA) Message Set Guidelines describe reporting fields and data relationships; they do not make the underlying import or audit records public. No access to non-public data or analysis of actual NOAA records is requested in response to this RFI. NMFS PGA Message Set Guidelines https://www.cbp.gov/document/guidance/nmfs-pga-message-set-guidelines Proposed milestones and billing approach NOAA is considering firm-fixed-price services with payments tied to Government acceptance of the following milestone outputs. The milestones, acceptance criteria, and payment terms are not final. Respondents should identify practical improvements. Milestone | Draft outputs I. Initial mapping and data development | Onboard, review existing work, and complete or refine initial supply-chain mapping, including source fisheries, landing locations, and primary processing entities. Provide a data table suitable for BigQuery and an electronic summary of the work completed and initial supply chains identified for further analysis. II. Prioritized supply chains | Develop the list of priority supply chains for further analysis, building on the Government-provided mapping. Provide the prioritization document and supporting documentation, including the source-fishery, landing, and primary-processing information used. III. Near-final mapping and analysis | Provide updated supply-chain mapping, analysis of priority supply chains, and re-import analysis. Include an updated BigQuery data table, supporting analytical materials, and research and summaries of source-fishery regulations and laws, including harvesting nations' legal species and harvesting methods relevant to U.S. imports. IV. Final reports and data | Complete internal and public reports with visuals, supporting documentation, and the final BigQuery data table containing supply-chain mapping and additional analysis. Reports and supporting documents are contemplated as electronic deliverables. Any hard-copy requirement would be specified in a solicitation. Information requested Provide a company information sheet and a narrative addressing the numbered questions on the following pages. Use the question numbers and state the assumptions behind each response. Brief, specific answers are preferred to general marketing materials.
